laws.citation: San Francisco Housing Code (minimum heat requirements, as amended January 20, 2020)
laws.title: Minimum heat requirements
laws.summary: Residential rental units (other than residential hotel rooms) must have a permanent heat source able to keep every habitable room at 70F, measured 3 feet above the floor; bathrooms and hallways are excluded. If the tenant does not control the heat, the landlord must provide it 24 hours a day. Residential hotel rooms must be kept at 68F for 13 hours a day: 5-11 AM and 3-10 PM. Portable heaters do not satisfy the requirement.
key_points: 70F in habitable rooms, measured 3 ft above floor
24 hours a day when landlord controls heat

laws.title: Residential noise limits and night construction
laws.summary: A person may not produce or allow noise from machines, devices, music or entertainment on residential property that exceeds the ambient level by more than 5 dBA at any point outside the property plane (§ 2909(a)(1)). Construction noise more than 5 dBA above ambient at the nearest property plane is prohibited between 8 PM and 7 AM without a special permit, except emergency work (§ 2908).
key_points: Residential: max 5 dBA above ambient at property plane
Night construction 8 PM-7 AM needs a permit
